clue.text: Puzzle seeing married male, strong beast, oppressed by what he calls a cold!

indicators.note: in a down clue, being oppressed means sitting underneath, so the other pieces come below

parts.note: the joke of 'man flu': a man calls his ordinary cold the flu
an ox is a powerful draught animal

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation about a husband who makes a huge fuss over a mere sniffle.
explanation.walkthrough: The gag is 'man flu': a man calls a cold flu. 'Oppressed by' in a down clue puts that piece on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To flummox someone is to baffle or bewilder them, a synonym of puzzle as a verb.

clue.text: Traitor after endless fortune — one has to be well-paid

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for fortune is dropped

parts.note: luck is good fortune
a rat is slang for a traitor or informer
I is the Roman numeral for one
've is the contracted form of have, as in I've

explanation.surface: A turncoat follows his luck, and someone must be paid well for the betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' gives the contraction of have, as in I've; 'endless' drops the last letter of the fortune word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucrative job is one that pays handsomely, so it describes being well-paid work.

clue.text: The woman loveless love put off

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: love is zero, the letter O, in tennis scoring, so loveless means with that letter removed

explanation.surface: A heartbroken woman, without love, has postponed romance altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' is the deletion instruction, taking O (love as zero in tennis) out of the following word 'love' to leave LVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to postpone or defer it, the same as putting it off.

clue.text: Prompt check on car — that is to save tax

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British cars

indicators.note: to save is to keep safe, so the words for that is hold the tax inside them

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A motorist's quick roadworthiness check, done so as to dodge some tax.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is the yearly safety test for British cars over three years old; VAT is Britain's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To motivate someone is to spur or encourage them to act, as a verb prompt does.

clue.text: False impression made by undertaking absorbing little program about chicken

indicators.note: absorbing means taking the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: a mission is a task or undertaking
an app is a small computer program, short for application
re means about or concerning
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: Someone's misunderstanding arose from a project that involved a small piece of software about poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts the three short pieces inside the word for undertaking, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A misapprehension is a mistaken belief or misunderstanding, which is a false impression.

clue.text: Reject that could show worth?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the letters of THROW thrown out (rearranged) could give the clue word worth

explanation.surface: Something discarded that might nonetheless have shown its value.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction, with OUT as the anagram signal on THROW, would produce the clue's word 'worth'.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out an idea or item is to discard it, the same as rejecting it.

clue.text: Circulation aids weathercocks, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals a word that is pronounced like another but spelt differently

parts.note: vanes are weathercocks, the devices that turn to show wind direction

explanation.surface: Weathercocks apparently help with circulation, presumably of air around a rooftop.
explanation.definitionFit: Veins are the blood vessels returning blood to the heart, so they help circulation.

clue.text: Having defeats and victories only, apparently, in an open-neck shirt?

definitions.text: Having defeats and victories only, apparently
definitions.meaning: a record of only wins and losses has no draws, which are ties
a man in an open-necked shirt wears no necktie

explanation.walkthrough: Ties are drawn games, so a team with only wins and losses has no ties, read as a pun on the answer's two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a necktie describes a man casually dressed in a shirt with an open collar.

clue.text: Power given by Irish water that produces agricultural turnover

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
a lough is an Irish lake or sea inlet

explanation.surface: Hydroelectric power from an Irish lake drives a farm's profitable business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like farm revenue but means soil being turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm implement that cuts and turns the soil over, so it literally turns the land.

clue.text: Tea-maker who tries really hard?

definitions.meaning: a sieve used when pouring loose-leaf tea, so a tool in tea-making
one who strains, exerting maximum effort

explanation.definitionFit: A sieve for tea leaves is the kitchen sense; someone making great efforts is the whimsical one.

clue.text: Blended label rum — one should keep water away

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so these letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: A rum sold under a blended label, which certainly isn't meant to be watered down.
explanation.definitionFit: A brolly is held up to keep rain off, so it keeps the wet away.

clue.text: Old rocker's following used to be dissipated

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece goes second

parts.note: was is the past tense of to be
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s rock-and-roll fan

explanation.surface: An ageing rock-and-roller's fan base has faded away.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys (Teds) were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits who loved rock and roll; 'Old rocker's' gives TED with ''s' read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissipated and wasted both describe something squandered, or someone spent by excess.

clue.text: Repress what head and tail of pups do?

definitions.meaning: to keep feelings in rather than letting them out

definitions.text: what head and tail of pups do?
definitions.meaning: an excited puppy's head and tail both go up, so said quickly 'both'll up'

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a playful sound-alike: both (head and tail) will go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep emotions suppressed and unexpressed is to repress them, an idiom.

clue.text: Most uneven nap, having eaten duck — that's horrid!

indicators.note: having eaten means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: a nap is a rest
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, the letter O
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A disgusted reaction to a nap taken after eating duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughest is the superlative of rough, meaning least smooth or level.

clue.text: House idly refurbished in a frightful way

indicators.note: refurbished means done up and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A house carelessly renovated ends up looking dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideously means in an ugly or horrible manner, synonymous with frightfully.

clue.text: I will join good number going to rave in the dark

parts.note: to rave is to rant

explanation.surface: Someone joins a group heading to a party held in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rave' looks like a dance party but means to rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark is an idiom for being uninformed, unaware or lacking knowledge.

clue.text: In great detail, eventually

definitions.meaning: fully and thoroughly, as in discussing something exhaustively

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both exhaustively and fully, and after a long wait, finally.

clue.text: Like a mere stain?

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake, as a mere is a lake
the suffix -ish means like or resembling

explanation.surface: A question whether a mere stain is all it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like 'only', but is a noun meaning lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to discolour or sully something, the same as to stain it.

clue.text: Half of school rejected studying sacred books by this writer, one inventing plots

indicators.note: half of picks out the first half of the word school
rejected means sent back, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject studying scripture
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A writer who turned down half his schooling in scripture devises plots.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is the British school subject studying scripture; 'rejected' turns it and the writer's pronoun round together, giving EMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A schemer is someone who devises plots and intrigues, a plotter.

clue.text: Doctor envied church grounds

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered in order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A doctor envied the church's grounds, perhaps its gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' looks like land but means reasons or proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds as in grounds for suspicion are the basis or proof, the same as evidence.

clue.text: Pay and enter with the wrong order!

indicators.note: putting the two words in the wrong order swaps the pair round

parts.note: to enter is to come in

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay up and come in, given in a muddled sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is money earned, so a salary or pay counts as income.

clue.text: It's left on Dec 24 by Santa and his reindeer, and grand to put around rhubarb

definitions.text: It's left on Dec 24 by Santa and his reindeer

indicators.note: put around means these two pieces are placed on either side of the nonsense word

parts.note: G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds
rhubarb is slang for nonsense, as is rot

explanation.surface: Santa's Christmas Eve departure, oddly combined with a recipe for rhubarb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhubarb' looks like the vegetable but is British slang for nonsense; 'grand' is slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's grotto is the department-store cave where he meets children, empty once he sets off on Christmas Eve.

clue.text: Melody that gives those people energy

parts.note: them refers to those people
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A tune that energises those who hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a principal melody in a piece of music, as in a theme tune.

clue.text: Out-of-the-way tipsy cuddles, ecstasy to be hugged

indicators.note: to be hugged means held inside the jumbled letters
tipsy means drunk and unsteady, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drunken cuddles fuelled by ecstasy, conducted somewhere private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' jumbles CUDDLES into SCLUDED, and 'to be hugged' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded spot is remote and private, just as an out-of-the-way place is.

clue.text: Learned folk will be polite, rational, internally …

indicators.note: internally means the letters are found within the words that come before

explanation.surface: Scholars will be courteous and reasonable at heart, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Literati are well-read, educated people, especially those devoted to literature.

clue.text: … more calm, sitting back in chauffeured limousine

indicators.note: back means the found letters are read from the end to the start
sitting in means the letters are seated within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: the learned are even more relaxed, lounging in a chauffeured car.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 24 across for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Milder means gentler or less harsh, comparative like more calm.

clue.text: Northern god missing nothing, consumed in menace

indicators.note: missing means the letter for nothing is lost from the god's name

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
nothing is zero, the letter O
eaten means consumed

explanation.surface: A thunder god, empty-handed and swallowed up by danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten is to menace, to warn of harm or intimidate.
